audit.why: Both available win-rate sources agree this is a near-even lane that Sejuani loses slightly (MC_WR_TABLES 49.39 over 490 games; the packet 46.92 over 211). Difficulty framing left as-is, though diff reads EVEN while breakdown.difficulty and report[14] read 'Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10'; that contradiction is in questionsForUser rather than guessed at.

Level 1 to Jax is right — he has Relentless Assault ramping from his first auto and Sejuani's Frost Armor only holds until she takes damage. Level 3 to Jax matches Counter Strike coming online. Level 6 as Skill matches Glacial Prison's 1300-range point-and-click stun arriving. No stage side changed; the captions and sides already agree here.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] and wants.foe[0] both said Jax activates Counter Strike to dodge Winter's Wrath. Riot's Counter Strike text is 'Jax's combat prowess allows him to dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies.' It dodges attacks — basic attacks — not abilities.
audit.why: This is the single most important thing a Sejuani can know in this lane and the page had it backwards. Winter's Wrath, Permafrost and Glacial Prison are abilities and land in full through an active Counter Strike; only her autos are eaten. A Sejuani told her W gets dodged will hold the exact ability she should be casting, then eat the stun for nothing. Played correctly, Counter Strike going up is the cue to stop auto-attacking and start casting.
audit.corrected: whys[2] and wants.foe[0] now state that Counter Strike eats autos while W and E go through it; breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t carry the same rule as the trade instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] and mid both quote 'Counter Strike's 8-second cooldown'. dosFull[2].d offers a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 seconds. It is never 8 at any rank, and 15 is its rank-2 value, not its rank-1 value. Eight seconds understates the punish window by more than half and tells a Sejuani to skip trades she has time to take.
audit.corrected: 17s at rank 1 falling to 9s at rank 5 now stated in whys[3], mid, dosFull[2].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page flagged that Jax's opener is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Empower is an auto-reset on a 7s rank-1 cooldown down to 3s. The damage arrives on the swing, not on the cast, so the visual cue a Sejuani should react to is the wind-up rather than the ability animation.

edits.before: His full Q-E-W combo comes online: he leaps onto you with Q, activates Counter Strike to dodge your W and stun you at the end, then bursts with Empowered W — you cannot win an extended trade into this sequence.
edits.after: His full combo lands: Leap Strike in, Counter Strike up, Empower reset out. Counter Strike dodges attacks and not abilities, so keep casting W and E through it and hold your autos — but the stun still beats any extended trade.

edits.before: Counter Strike's 8-second cooldown creates brief trade windows for both sides but neither of you can land a full kill combo reliably — play for Frost stacks and disengage.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17 seconds at rank 1, not eight — that is a long punish window on both sides, but neither of you lands a full kill combo here, so play for Frost stacks and disengage.

edits.before: Activate Counter Strike the instant you throw W's first strike, then stun you mid-combo and follow with Q burst
edits.after: Pop Counter Strike as you swing so your autos are safe, then stun you mid-combo and follow with an Empower reset

edits.before: Stack Frost with W's two strikes safely from distance, then E-stun only when Counter Strike has just ended
edits.after: Keep casting W and E while Counter Strike is up — it eats autos, not abilities — and hold your basics until it drops

edits.before: Jax's Q leap into Counter Strike stun is his first all-in window — any extended trade he lands from level 3 with E up will hurt you badly.
edits.after: Jax's Leap Strike into Counter Strike is his first all-in, and Empower is an auto reset — react to the swing wind-up, not the cast.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are a neutral farm window where neither of you has a decisive edge if you respect Counter Strike's 8-second cooldown — watch for the glowing ring, trade only in the gap after it ends, and disengage with W's slow before it comes back up. At level 6 the lane flips back into a real threat for Jax: Trinity Force components make his burst spike sharply, but your Glacial Prison changes the equation. If he ever overextends or tries to shove without Counter Strike, throw R from max range to stun him in place and chain the E Permafrost — that combo either kills him outright or forces a flash. Never use R as a lane poke tool; bank it for when his E is visibly on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are a neutral farm window if you respect Counter Strike properly: it is 17 seconds at rank 1 and only 9 at rank 5, so the early punish window is long. Watch for the glowing ring, and remember it dodges attacks and not abilities — while it is up, stop auto-attacking and keep flailing W for Frost stacks, then disengage on the slow before it returns. At level 6 the lane sharpens for Jax as Trinity Force components land, but Glacial Prison changes the equation. If he shoves without Counter Strike, throw R from 1300 range to freeze him and chain Permafrost — that either kills him or takes his Flash. Never use R as lane poke; bank it for when his E is visibly down.

edits.before: Jax burns Counter Strike on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Jax burns Counter Strike on nothing — a seventeen-second invitation at rank 1.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your Q dash like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1 down to 9s. Dodges attacks, not abilities: while it is up, stop autoing and keep casting W and E. - Guard your Q dash like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Jax’s Counter Strike: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Counter Strike, 17s at rank 1: it eats your autos but not Winter's Wrath or Permafrost. Cast through it, swing after.

edits.before: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Dodges every auto but no abilities — keep casting W and E through it, and hold your basics until the ring goes out.
